summary.en: Switch matches one integer controlling value.
summary.bn: case, default আর break দিয়ে নির্দিষ্ট integer মানের জন্য কাজ বেছে নাও।

notes: The C17 examples use conventional case labels and comments for intended shared cases. C23 adds facilities such as standardized fallthrough attributes and permits more label placements. Those additions do not make accidental fall-through a good menu design.

examples.title: An exact menu selection
examples.explanationHtml: Choice two starts at case two, prints Help and leaves through break. The source order of case one does not make its message print first. Switch selection jumps directly to the matching label.

examples.title: Two labels share one action
examples.explanationHtml: Cases six and seven intentionally share the same statement. There is no work between their labels to fall through accidentally. Other values select the default class plan. The labels describe this lesson scheduling example, rather than a universal calendar policy.

examples.title: A small character calculator
examples.explanationHtml: Input selects subtraction with a character case label. The code subtracts four from nine and prints five. Each arithmetic case ends with break, and the division case checks zero separately. Unknown operation characters reach the default message.

practice.title: Three menu choices
practice.statementHtml: Read choice 0 to 9. After the prompt Input: , print Start for 1, Help for 2, otherwise Unknown; end the line.
hints: Each independent action needs an exit.

practice.title: Grouped labels
practice.statementHtml: Read level 0 to 5. After the prompt Input: , print Basic for 1 or 2, Other for any remaining value; end the line.
hints: Stack labels before one shared action.

practice.title: Character classification by choice
practice.statementHtml: Read one non-whitespace character. After the prompt Input: , print Add for +, Subtract for -, otherwise Other; end with newline.
hints: Character constants are integer constants in C.

practice.title: Four-operation integer calculator
practice.statementHtml: Read a, an operation character and b, with a and b from -100 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print the integer result for +, -, * or /. For / with zero b print Zero divisor. For another operation print Unknown. End each result with newline.
hints: Select the operation, then guard its arithmetic.

quiz.prompt: What kind of controlling expression does C switch accept?
quiz.explanation: Character and enum values fit through integer rules.

quiz.prompt: What must a case label contain?
quiz.explanation: The label values are determined during translation.

quiz.prompt: What happens after a case action without a control transfer?
quiz.explanation: Case labels do not block fall-through.

quiz.prompt: Which statement normally ends one independent case?
quiz.explanation: Break leaves the nearest switch or loop.
Default is an optional unmatched-value fallback.

May case 10 and case 0xA coexist in one switch?
quiz.explanation: Case uniqueness is based on converted integer values.

quiz.prompt: Case two breaks before default. Which message appears?
quiz.explanation: The matching case prints then break leaves.

Two labels share one action. Which text prints for 1?
quiz.explanation: The stacked labels reach a single output statement.

examQuestions.question: Read a, an operation character and b, with a and b from -100 to 100. After Input: print the integer result for +, -, * or /. For / with zero b print Zero divisor. For another operation print Unknown. End each result with newline.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int a, b;
    char operation;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d %c %d", &a, &operation, &b) != 3
        || a < -100 || a > 100 || b < -100 || b > 100) {
        return 1;
    }
    switch (operation) {
        case '+':
            printf("%d\n", a + b);
            break;
        case '-':
            printf("%d\n", a - b);
            break;
        case '*':
            printf("%d\n", a * b);
            break;
        case '/':
            if (b == 0) {
                puts("Zero divisor");
            } else {
                printf("%d\n", a / b);
            }
            break;
        default:
            puts("Unknown");
            break;
    }
    return 0;
}
